data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 conflates organizational independence with implementation heterogeneity, then smuggles the latter in as the load-bearing mechanism. Its own counterconditions concede that mandated frameworks and shared critical dependencies invalidate the claim — i.e., when small operators are independently run but homogeneous (precisely the common real-world case), the 'blast radius' decoupling vanishes. Under the problem's regime, 'one large service with strictly more total internal redundancy' can architecturally partition its redundant nodes across diverse stacks, deployment schedules, and infrastructures; its strictly greater redundancy can therefore achieve at least the same circuit-breaker effect SRC_001 attributes only to decentralization. No evidence is offered that a decentralized network can guarantee the implementation diversity its mechanism requires, so the resilience claim is unsupported against the stated comparator.
